newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Gidusa to boost production.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Gidusa to boost production.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Industrial Durango (Gidusa) expects to boost production of paper and packaging products over the coming five years in line with growing domestic demand, a company director told Reuters.
"We closed 1996 with record full-year (production) figures and seek to consolidate our position and double the firm's value by the year 2000," Gidusa Chief Financial Officer Mayela Velasco said.

"Demand for packaging in Mexico is expected to increase at 12 percent per year over the next five years, which would allow Gidusa to increase output from seven million square feet to 12 million by the year 2000," she added.

Gidusa posted record production figures in 1996, which were up 16 percent from 1995. Velasco said operating earnings increased by two percent to $87.5 million despite a real fall of two percent in prices.
Nonetheless, Velasco said "we expect a price increase shortly" for egg boxes, multilayered bags and molded boxes, which account for 90 percent of the firm's revenues.
"We expected a price hike of 20-25 percent for recycled products over the year as a whole, but that will depend on international market prices for paper," she said.
"We have already raised corrugated box prices by 10 percent of an announced 15 percent, and expect to apply the remaining five percent next year," Velasco said.
Some 12 percent of Gidusa's costs are denominated in dollars, she added.
Gidusa is running at 95 percent of its production capacity for paper and 80 percent for packaging, Velasco said.
Gidusa has set aside $8-10 million to spend on plant maintenance and a similar amount for internal expansion plans, she said.

Velasco said Gidusa also aims to install new packaging plants in the United States in order to bolster its presence among manufacturers along the U.S.-Mexico border, although the firm has no finalized plans as yet.
